New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-embedded-filter-card-brands-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-embedded-filter-card-brands-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-embedded-filter-card-brands.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded-filter-card-brands`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded-filter-card-brands identifies card-brand choice and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The detailed 2026-04-22 guide assumes a Stripe account and an existing Mobile Embedded Payment Element integration. Its client configuration can allow only listed brands or disallow them, and shows a Visa/Mastercard allow list. The four categories are Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover, with Discover covering its global network including Diners Club, JCB, UnionPay and Elo (old raw lines 12-52, old raw lines 63-128 and old raw lines 139-190). The configuration belongs to the Embedded Element. Android and React Native examples refer to PaymentSheet brand types, and the April Swift example sets the Embedded configuration. The mapped source-stripe-inapp-embedded-filter-card-brands.md preserves those mechanics but calls Apple Pay an all-platform feature. The April Android Embedded wording repeats Apple Pay, while the related April Android Embedded integration documents Google Pay setup and leaves the actual Google Pay filter scope unverified (`raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:4423-4447`). The retained SDKs describe client-side filtering. The April checkout test suggestions provide a way to test a filter, and the captures do not show a successful payment or a server authorization rule (old raw lines 130-133 and old raw lines 192-195).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded-filter-card-brands, November is presentation and navigation to the same platform variants (new raw lines 9-15). source-stripe-inapp-embedded-filter-card-brands.md and the reciprocal in-app concept should keep April's allow/disallow semantics, brand categories, prerequisites and platform examples dated (old raw lines 12-52, old raw lines 63-128 and old raw lines 139-190). The Android Apple Pay line conflicts with the dated Android PaymentSheet Google Pay line and Embedded Google Pay setup, while the retained React Native SDK scopes Apple Pay to iOS and Google Pay to Android (`raw/stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands-2025.md:63-82`, `raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:4423-4447`, React Native snapshot 2026-10-29-33ef1ee `EmbeddedPaymentElement.tsx:133-145`). Wallet setup does not prove an Embedded Google Pay network-filter outcome. On iOS StripePaymentSheet 26.11.0 uses a distinct Embedded configuration with aliases to the PaymentSheet brand type, so the April namespace table needs a version qualification (snapshot 2026-09-30-7037819, `EmbeddedPaymentElement.swift:593-611`, `PaymentSheetConfiguration.swift:846-871`). The retained iOS and React Native interfaces call the feature client-side and exclude Link. React Native 0.84.0's Android mapping falls back to all brands for a missing list or one with no recognized brands, while iOS maps a provided array even if empty (snapshot 2026-10-29-33ef1ee, `PaymentElementConfig.kt:220-253`, `StripeSdkImpl+PaymentSheet.swift:261-299`). Keep those package-specific boundaries apart from a server acceptance policy, a universal compatibility minimum, and actual payment execution.
